record.paper_title: Ordered Banach algebras and multi-norms: some open problems
record.original_question: If A is a Banach lattice algebra that is not Dedekind complete, can it be embedded in a Dedekind complete Banach lattice superalgebra B in such a way that every lattice algebra homomorphism from A into a Dedekind complete Banach lattice algebra C extends uniquely to a lattice algebra homomorphism from B into C ? A candidate construction for such B might consist of the Dedekind completion of A with a judicious choice of extensions of the norm and multiplication on A , but it is not even clear whether this can always be done so as to make B a Banach lattice algebra.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A Banach lattice algebra is a real associative algebra $A$ equipped with a vector lattice (Riesz space) structure and a complete lattice norm $\|\cdot\|$ such that:
(i) $\|\cdot\|$ is submultiplicative, i.e. $\|ab\| \le \|a\|\,\|b\|$ for all $a,b \in A$;
(ii) the product of two positive elements is positive, i.e. $a,b \ge 0$ implies $ab \ge 0$.
A Banach lattice algebra $A$ is called Dedekind complete if every nonempty order-bounded subset of $A$ has a supremum.

A lattice algebra homomorphism between Banach lattice algebras is an algebra homomorphism that is also a lattice (Riesz) homomorphism (it need not be assumed continuous a priori; equivalently, one may restrict attention to the continuous ones).

Question: Suppose $A$ is a Banach lattice algebra that is not Dedekind complete. Does there exist a Dedekind complete Banach lattice algebra $B$ together with an isometric lattice algebra embedding $\iota : A \hookrightarrow B$ with the following universal property: for every Dedekind complete Banach lattice algebra $C$ and every lattice algebra homomorphism $\varphi : A \to C$, there exists a unique lattice algebra homomorphism $\tilde{\varphi} : B \to C$ such that $\tilde{\varphi} \circ \iota = \varphi$?

In particular, can the underlying vector-lattice Dedekind completion of $A$ always be endowed with an extension of the norm and of the multiplication of $A$ so as to become a Banach lattice algebra?
artifact.status_search_result: The problem is posed as an open question in the literature on Banach lattice algebras. A web search did not surface any paper announcing a positive or negative resolution; related work addresses only partial aspects (e.g., representation of Banach lattice algebras as regular operators, or Dedekind completions of normed lattices without algebra structure). No solution found.

status_evidence.title: Banach lattice algebras: some questions, but very few answers
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of open questions on Banach lattice algebras, including representation and completion issues.
status_evidence.claim: Several basic structural questions about Banach lattice algebras, including completion-type questions, remain open.

status_evidence.title: On Normed Lattices and Their Banach Completions
status_evidence.snippet: Banach completion of a normed lattice need not preserve Dedekind completeness.
status_evidence.claim: Related completion procedures are subtle and do not automatically yield Dedekind complete Banach lattices.
